findings.text: follow-on: the goal's stated mechanism did not deliver the goal's stated effect. The node goal is 'make the read valid AND near-linear at 10,000 cells BY bounding its component-label propagation'. The bounding change (pointer-hooking + parent halving, round_limit 4*bit_length) is real and reduces label rounds from 99 (one-hop, job 1283227, label_rounds 99) to 8 (job 1283224, limited 10000), so it does bound the propagation. But the read wall is dominated by other stages: the fitted log-log warm-wall exponent is 1.479 (limited) / 1.458 (diverted) against the base one-hop exponent 1.472, and the 10,000-cell warm wall is 80.623 s versus the base 79. The node measures and states this itself (fragment cfs-read-ten-thousand-labels; 'bounding the propagation did not reduce the read wall'), and assigns near-linearity to a later read-wall node. The validity at 10,000 cells is produced not by the propagation change but by the membership-admission change: restoring one-hop propagation WITH the new admission bound stays valid=True (job 1283227, limited 10000, reason 0). So one of the two named goal properties and the named mechanism that was to produce the other did not land; the node's honest disclosure is why this is a follow-on rather than a blocking finding.

follow-on: the membership admission band was decoupled from its policy operand. Before the change the band was policy.edge_tolerance (TopologyPolicy default 1.0e-12, solve_request.py:247); after the change read() uses _membership_roundoff_bound(area, geometry) = 4 * finfo(area.dtype).eps * 32 * 3 * (3*vertices+1) * capacity, a computed constant, and policy.edge_tolerance no longer governs the membership band at all (it remains used only for _wall_events and the label edge tolerance). A caller that tightened edge_tolerance to catch overfills no longer affects this band. The relaxation is defensible on the numbers (base raw_max 1.0000000000015354, overshoot 1.5354e-12, allowance 4.77485e-12, ~3.1x margin; a 1e-8 injected overfill is still refused and the floating-point identity goldens are unchanged), but it is a semantic weakening of a policy-controlled guard that the node did not call out.

follow-on: the manifest's declared negative control was falsified by the node's own later measurement, and the named log substitutes a different mutation with no note. The prompt declared the negative-control string 'restoring the base label propagation reproduces UNRESOLVED_COMPONENT at 10,000 cells by test id'. The node's own timing control (job 1283227, propagation=one-hop, limited 10000) shows the restored base propagation WITH the committed admission bound returns valid=True, reason=0 — i.e. the declared string is false at the reviewed head, because the base refusal at 10,000 cells was the membership check, not the propagation. The manifest names negative_control_log = overfill-negative.log, which is a DIFFERENT mutation (admission_control.py disabling _membership_roundoff_bound), failing the different id test_large_membership.../test_large_membership_overfill_is_refused. That log is admitted on its own facts (EXIT=1, a failing id the head arm does not fail) and I reproduced it, but the record's negative_control_log does not correspond to the declared string and no negative_control_note records why. The declared mutation's evidence lives in baseline_suite's base arm (reason=7 at 10000-limited), not in the named file.

justifications.call_sites: Four call sites, all updated and all in scope; the private helper's contract change from two to four return values reaches no production caller beyond _support_at_level and the prototype monkeypatch, both updated. No out-of-scope caller break analogous to a signature change missed elsewhere.
justifications.durability: The guards are real and falsifiable, and I reproduced the falsification at the reviewed head: the membership refusal test passes at head (2 passed with the long-path test, review-head-fast.log EXIT=0) and the declared guard-disable mutation makes it fail by id (admission_control.py, review-negctl.log, 'FAILED ...test_large_membership_overfill_is_refused', EXIT=1), matching the node's overfill-negative.log to the failing id. The identity contract is pinned by twelve committed base snapshots. Below the top band for three reasons: the membership admission band was decoupled from policy.edge_tolerance (TopologyPolicy.edge_tolerance default 1e-12 no longer governs it), silently weakening a policy-controlled guard; the head suite arm predates the reviewed head (docs-only, so latent); and the manifest's arm commands do not carry the output argument the logs record, so the 'literal runnable command' does not reproduce the named log paths.
justifications.evidence: Independently reproduced, not read. This review re-ran the two fast tests at the reviewed head (review-head-fast.log: 'test_fragment_representatives_converge_across_long_paths' and 'test_large_membership_overfill_is_refused', 2 passed in 27.38 s, EXIT=0) and re-ran the declared guard-disable mutation (review-negctl.log: EXIT=1, failing id the head arm passes). Read from the run's own logs rather than re-run (heavy, H200): the two suite arms (base 2 failed/8 passed + 3 passed; head 10 passed + 3 passed), the ladder rows for both cases at all four rungs (job 1283224 limited, job 1283227 diverted+one-hop control), the CPU identity six-row gate (6 passed, 2 deselected), the base diagnosis (reason=7, raw_max 1.0000000000015354, 29 outside cells), and the CPU 10,000 snapshot (valid, warm 33.044 s). The fragment is audit-conformant (reckon audit 0 findings). Verified the enum reason=7 == TopologyReason.UNRESOLVED_COMPONENT and that the two post-suite commits are fragment-only.
justifications.fit: Follows the done-when closely: pointer-hooking plus parent-halving is exactly the 'pointer doubling or union by halving' the clause names, and the read's kernel stages the brief fenced (_sampled_flux, _null_census, _curvature_derivatives, _wall_events) are untouched. The change reuses the read's own path and the ladder prototype. Two deductions: the mechanism the goal names did not fit the observed bottleneck (the wall is not the propagation), and the membership band was moved off its policy operand onto a computed constant without the design asking for it.
justifications.goal_fidelity: Half landed. Validity at 10,000 cells is achieved for both analytic cases (valid=True, reason=0; H200 head arm 10 passed; fragment wall table all 'yes'), and the propagation bound is real (rounds 99 -> 8). Near-linearity is not achieved: warm wall 80.623 s (limited) / 74.792 s (diverted) at 10,000 versus 1.124 / 1.091 s at 550, fitted exponents 1.479 / 1.458 against the base 1.472, i.e. the throughput is essentially unchanged by the change. The node measures this and reports it ('the measured wall is an open follow-on', meta plan-summary and follow_ons), which is why the deduction stops at partial rather than failing the node.
justifications.reuse: No parallel mechanism. The read path, the analytic fixture helpers (_analytic_inputs, _realised_hex_geometry, _reference_cell_fractions in tests/equilibrium/test_topology_read.py, unchanged and outside the diff), the compatibility goldens, and the existing ladder prototype are all reused; the only new product code is the rewritten _connected_fragment_labels and the ~10-line _membership_roundoff_bound helper. Backend-qualified snapshots (-cpu suffix) key the identity to the backend that produced the measure rather than assuming cross-backend equality.
